d.t: Expression of hesitation, uncertainty or space filler in conversation.
d.e: Um, I don’t know.

d.t: Dated spelling of mmm.
d.e: "About the same, wherever you go," he agreed. "Um," I said.

d.t: An expression to forcefully call attention to something wrong.
d.e: Um, excuse me!

d.t: An expression of shocked disapproval used by a child who witnesses forbidden behavior.
d.e: While I was in her room, Sam walked by and said, “Um, I'm telling!” “You're telling what?” I asked. “You're reading Tori's journal,” she said.

d.t: To make the um sound to express uncertainty or hesitancy.
d.e: Meanwhile, in the popular mind umming was simply a bad habit, akin to spitting or picking one’s nose.

d.t: An occurrence of the interjection "um".
d.e: Although Shakespeare refers to “hums and ha’s,” sifting through etiquette manuals and public-speaking guides turns up scant evidence of a prohibition against ums, ers and uhs, which are profuse in the first recording of Thomas Edison’s voice, in 1888. Mr. Erard, rather…

d.t: An undifferentiated determiner or article; a miscellaneous linking word, or filler with nonspecific meaning; representation of broken English stereotypically or comically attributed to Native Americans.
d.e: Me be Injun. Him um Growling Bear. Him um heap big chief.

d.t: Any of the horse girl characters from Umamusume.
d.e: Agnes Tachyon is my favorite Uma.

d.t: One of the five basic tastes, the savory taste of foods such as seaweed, cured fish, aged cheeses and meats.
d.e: Umami is the mysterious “fifth taste”—a flavour that has never seemed to fit into the existing categories of sweet, sour, salty and bitter. South-east Asian chefs have exploited it throughout history—it's an essential part of the taste of seaweed, among other things[…]

d.t: A member of a Sahaptin-speaking Native American tribe who traditionally inhabited the Columbia Plateau region of the northwestern United States, along the Umatilla and Columbia rivers.
Of or relating to the Umayyad dynasty, which ruled the Umayyad Caliphate from Damascus between 661 and 744 then from Harran until 750, and al-Andalus between 756 and 1031.
A member of the Umayyad dynasty.
A flat-topped or rounded flower-cluster (= inflorescence) in which the individual flower stalks arise from the same point, the youngest flowers being at the centre.

d.t: To give a reddish-brown colour to.
d.e: Armies o'er armies heap'd, the locusts came, Like clouds in autumn umbering all the sky […]

Supported by a central stalk.
A navel.

The central region of a sunspot.
A shadow.

d.t: A feeling of anger or annoyance caused by something offensive.
d.e: Antipathy in one nation against another disposes each more readily to offer insult and injury, to lay hold of slight causes of umbrage, and to be haughty and intractable when accidental or trifling occasions of dispute occur.

d.t: A feeling of doubt.
Leaves that provide shade, as the foliage of trees.

d.t: Shadow; shade.
d.e: […] but in the verity of extolment I take him to be a soul of great article and his infusion of such dearth and rareness as, to make true diction of him, his semblable in his mirror, and who else would trace him, his umbrage, nothing more.

d.t: To displease or cause offense.
To shade.
Of or relating to an umbra.
Of or relating to umbral calculus.
A cloth-covered frame used for protection against rain or sun.
d.e: Quick, grab that umbrella before you get rained on!

d.t: Anything that provides similar protection.
d.e: The fighters provide a defensive air umbrella over the battle group.

d.t: Anything that provides similar overarching coverage of a range of concepts, purposes, groups, etc.
d.e: The test facility was established under the umbrella of the company's quality program.

d.t: A strategy in which five players in the offensive zone form an umbrella-shaped formation around the opposition's goal net.
The main body of a jellyfish, excluding the tentacles.
d.e: Jellyfish are composed of more than 90% water and most of their umbrella mass is made up of gelatinous material.

d.t: An umbrella-shaped reflector with a white or silvery inner surface, used to diffuse a nearby light.
d.e: Using umbrellas for shooting a wedding party is ok, but not necessary.

d.t: To cover or protect, as if by an umbrella.
d.e: Experts with saws and ladders came and lopped off the lower branches. This sent the tree's growth rushing violently to her head in a lush overhanging which umbrellaed the House of All Sorts.

d.t: To form the dome shape of an open umbrella.
d.e: Bright yellow gowns fit them tightly and umbrellaed from their waist to just below the knees.

d.t: To move like a jellyfish.
d.e: The light catches the filigreed tendrils and graceful motion of the jellies, their orange bodies umbrella-ing along like fairy parasols come to life.

d.t: Of, from or relating to Umbria, Italy or the extinct Umbrian language.

d.e: […] Gauls used the suffix -acus, Etruscans -nas or -na, Umbrians -enus, -ienus.

d.t: Chinese plum, a species of Asian plum, Prunus mume.
Pickled ume fruits.

d.t: The environs of a city, town, or village that are part of the main community through common economic and cultural activities.
An assimilatory process whereby a vowel is pronounced more like a following vocoid that is separated by one or more consonants.
d.e: In fits of concealed despair that went unnoticed even by those close enough to touch, Julien cursed the language of umlauts, eszetts, and gerunds.

d.t: The umlaut process (as above) that occurred historically in Germanic languages whereby back vowels became front vowels when followed by syllable containing a front vocoid (e.g. Germanic lūsiz > Old English lȳs(i) > Modern English lice).
A vowel so assimilated.
The diacritical mark ( ¨ ) placed over a vowel when it indicates a (rounded) front vowel
Synonym of diaeresis.
d.e: "Naïve" takes an umlaut because it is pronounced as two syllables.

d.t: To place an umlaut over (a vowel).

d.e: an umlauting vowel

To decide as an umpire.
